title: Two Sum
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target. Assume exactly one solution exists.
approachHint: Use a hash map to store each number's index as you iterate. Check if (target - num) exists in the map.

title: Maximum Subarray (Kadane's Algorithm)
statement: Find the contiguous subarray within an integer array which has the largest sum and return its sum.
approachHint: Maintain currentSum = max(num, currentSum + num) and update globalMax at each step.

title: Rotate Array by K Steps
statement: Given an integer array nums, rotate the array to the right by k steps, where k is non-negative.
approachHint: Reverse the entire array, then reverse the first k elements, then reverse the remaining n-k elements.

title: Merge Overlapping Intervals
statement: Given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [starti, endi], merge all overlapping intervals into non-overlapping intervals.
approachHint: Sort intervals by start time. Compare current interval with the last merged interval's end time.

title: Product of Array Except Self
statement: Return an array output such that output[i] is equal to the product of all elements of nums except nums[i], without using division.
approachHint: Calculate prefix products in forward pass, then multiply suffix products in backward pass.

title: Majority Element (> n/2 times)
statement: Given an array nums of size n, return the majority element that appears more than ⌊n / 2⌋ times.
approachHint: Boyer-Moore Voting Algorithm: maintain candidate and count. Increment if match, decrement if mismatch.

title: Subarray Sum Equals K
statement: Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, return the total number of subarrays whose sum equals to k.
approachHint: Use running prefix sum hash map storing frequencies of cumulative sums seen so far.

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
statement: Given an unsorted array of integers nums, return the length of the longest consecutive elements sequence in O(n) time.
approachHint: Insert elements into a Hash Set. Only start counting sequence from numbers that don't have (num - 1) in the set.

title: Valid Anagram
statement: Given two strings s and t, return true if t is an anagram of s, and false otherwise.
approachHint: Use a frequency array of size 26. Increment count for chars in s and decrement for chars in t.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
statement: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
approachHint: Sliding window with hash map storing most recent index of each character.

title: Palindromic Substrings Count
statement: Given a string s, return the number of palindromic substrings in it.
approachHint: Expand around center for each index for both odd and even length centers.

title: String Compression (Run-Length)
statement: Compress an array of characters in-place using the counts of repeated characters.
approachHint: Two-pointer approach: read consecutive identical characters, write character and its count.

title: Group Anagrams
statement: Given an array of strings strs, group the anagrams together in any order.
approachHint: Use character frequency tuple (or sorted string) as hash map key.

title: Minimum Window Substring
statement: Given strings s and t, return the minimum window substring of s such that every character in t is included in the window.
approachHint: Sliding window with two frequency maps and a 'formed' variable tracking fulfilled unique character counts.

title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
statement: Given a 1-indexed sorted array of integers numbers, find two numbers such that they add up to target.
approachHint: Left pointer at start, right at end. Move left if sum < target, right if sum > target.

title: 3Sum Zero Triplet
statement: Find all unique triplets [nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]] such that i != j != k and nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0.
approachHint: Sort array. Fix first element, then use two pointers for remaining two. Skip duplicates carefully.

title: Container With Most Water
statement: Given an integer array height of length n, find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container containing the most water.
approachHint: Two pointers at both ends. Compute area, then move the pointer with smaller height inward.

title: Trapping Rain Water
statement: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
approachHint: Two pointers with leftMax and rightMax, advance the pointer with smaller max boundary.

title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
statement: You are given a string s and an integer k. Choose any character and change it up to k times. Return length of longest substring with same letter.
approachHint: Sliding window tracking maxFrequency. If (windowLength - maxFreq) > k, shrink from left.

title: Reverse a Linked List
statement: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list, and return the reversed list.
approachHint: Iterate with three pointers: prev = null, curr = head, nextTemp. Reassign curr.next = prev.

title: Detect Cycle in Linked List
statement: Given head of a linked list, determine if the list has a cycle in it.
approachHint: Floyd's Tortoise and Hare algorithm: slow moves 1 step, fast moves 2 steps. They meet if cycle exists.

title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
statement: Merge two sorted linked lists and return it as a sorted list. The list should be made by splicing together the nodes of the first two lists.
approachHint: Use a dummy head node. Compare values of l1 and l2, appending smaller node to merged list.

title: Find Middle of the Linked List
statement: Given the head of a singly linked list, return the middle node of the linked list.
approachHint: Fast pointer moves two steps while slow pointer moves one step. When fast reaches end, slow is at middle.

title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
statement: Given the head of a linked list, remove the nth node from the end of the list and return its head.
approachHint: Advance fast pointer n steps ahead, then advance slow and fast together until fast reaches end.

title: LRU Cache Design
statement: Design a data structure that follows the constraints of a Least Recently Used (LRU) cache with get and put in O(1) time.
approachHint: Combine a Doubly Linked List with a Hash Map mapping keys to node pointers.

title: Valid Parentheses
statement: Given a string s containing '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid.
approachHint: Push opening brackets onto stack. For closing brackets, pop and check if matching bracket type.

title: Min Stack Implementation
statement: Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element in constant time O(1).
approachHint: Store pairs (val, currentMin) or maintain a separate parallel stack of minimum values.

title: Next Greater Element
statement: Find the first greater element to the right for each element in an array. If no greater element exists, return -1.
approachHint: Monotonic decreasing stack: iterate from right to left, popping elements smaller than current.

title: Implement Queue using Two Stacks
statement: Implement a first in first out (FIFO) queue using only two standard LIFO stacks.
approachHint: Push onto stack1. For pop/peek, transfer from stack1 to stack2 if stack2 is empty.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
statement: Given an array nums and window size k, return the max element in each sliding window of size k.
approachHint: Use a Monotonic Deque storing indices, maintaining elements in decreasing order.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
statement: Given an integer array nums sorted in ascending order and rotated at an unknown pivot, find index of target in O(log n).
approachHint: Determine which half (left or right) is sorted. Check if target lies within that sorted range.

title: Find First and Last Position of Element
statement: Given an array of integers nums sorted in non-decreasing order, find the starting and ending position of a given target value.
approachHint: Run two modified binary searches: one finding lower bound, one finding upper bound.

title: Square Root Integer Function
statement: Given a non-negative integer x, return the square root of x rounded down to the nearest integer without built-in functions.
approachHint: Binary search in range [1, x]. If mid * mid <= x, record mid as answer and search right half.

title: Find Peak Element
statement: A peak element is an element strictly greater than its neighbors. Find index of any peak element in O(log n).
approachHint: If nums[mid] < nums[mid + 1], peak must lie in right half; otherwise it lies in left half.

title: Capacity To Ship Packages Within D Days
statement: Find the least weight capacity of the ship that will result in all packages being shipped within days D.
approachHint: Binary search on answer between max(weights) and sum(weights). Check feasibility greedily.

title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
statement: Given the root of a binary tree, return the level order traversal of its nodes' values (from left to right, level by level).
approachHint: BFS using a queue. Track queue.length at start of each iteration to capture entire level.

title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
statement: Given the root of a binary tree, return its maximum depth (number of nodes along longest path).
approachHint: Post-order recursive DFS: 1 + max(depth(node.left), depth(node.right)).

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
statement: Given the root of a binary tree, determine if it is a valid binary search tree (BST).
approachHint: DFS passing valid ranges (minVal, maxVal). Left child range (minVal, node.val), right child (node.val, maxVal).

title: Lowest Common Ancestor in BST
statement: Given a binary search tree (BST), find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) node of two given nodes p and q.
approachHint: If both p and q are smaller than root, traverse left; if both greater, traverse right; else root is LCA.

title: Diameter of Binary Tree
statement: Return length of longest path between any two nodes in a tree. This path may or may not pass through root.
approachHint: At each node, compute max height of left and right. Update maxDiameter with leftHeight + rightHeight.

title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
statement: Design an algorithm to serialize a binary tree to a string and deserialize that string back to the original tree.
approachHint: Preorder traversal with delimiters and marker 'null' for missing children.

title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
statement: Given the root of a binary search tree, and an integer k, return the kth smallest value (1-indexed) of all values of the nodes.
approachHint: Inorder traversal visits BST elements in strictly ascending sorted order. Decrement k until k == 0.

title: Path Sum Equals Target
statement: Given root and targetSum, return true if tree has root-to-leaf path such that adding all values equals targetSum.
approachHint: Recursively check left and right subtrees with targetSum - node.val. True if leaf reached with 0 remainder.

title: Number of Islands
statement: Given an m x n 2D binary grid grid which represents a map of '1's (land) and '0's (water), return the number of islands.
approachHint: Iterate through cells. When '1' found, increment count and trigger DFS/BFS sink to '0' for all connected land.

title: Clone Graph
statement: Given a reference of a node in a connected undirected graph, return a deep copy (clone) of the graph.
approachHint: Use a Hash Map mapping original nodes to cloned nodes. Traverse with DFS or BFS creating missing clones.

title: Course Schedule (Topological Sort / Cycle)
statement: There are numCourses courses labeled 0 to numCourses - 1. Determine if you can finish all courses given prerequisite pairs.
approachHint: Kahn's Algorithm using in-degree array and queue, or DFS with 3-state visited array (0=unvisited, 1=visiting, 2=visited).

title: Dijkstra's Shortest Path Algorithm
statement: Given a weighted directed graph and source node, find shortest distances from source to all vertices.
approachHint: Min-Heap priority queue storing (distance, node). Greedily expand shortest unvisited node.

title: Number of Connected Components (Disjoint Set Union)
statement: Find number of connected components in an undirected graph with n nodes and edge list.
approachHint: Union-Find with path compression and union by rank. Decrement component count upon successful union.

title: Word Ladder (Shortest Transformation)
statement: Given two words (beginWord and endWord) and a dictionary wordList, return the length of the shortest transformation sequence.
approachHint: Bidirectional BFS: expand from both beginWord and endWord, checking one-letter mutations against wordSet.

title: Rotting Oranges (Multi-Source BFS)
statement: Return minimum minutes until no fresh orange remains in grid. If impossible, return -1.
approachHint: Multi-source BFS: enqueue all initially rotten oranges. Spread rot level by level, decrementing fresh count.

title: Climbing Stairs
statement: You are climbing a staircase with n steps. Each time you can climb 1 or 2 steps. In how many distinct ways can you climb to the top?
approachHint: Fibonacci recurrence: dp[i] = dp[i - 1] + dp[i - 2]. Store only last two states.

title: House Robber
statement: Determine max amount of money you can rob tonight without alerting the police (cannot rob two adjacent houses).
approachHint: At each house i, choose max(rob(i-1), rob(i-2) + nums[i]). Space optimize to two variables.

title: Coin Change (Fewest Coins)
statement: Given coins of different denominations and total amount, compute the fewest number of coins needed to make up that amount.
approachHint: Bottom-up 1D DP array of size (amount + 1). dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[i - coin] + 1) for each coin.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS)
statement: Given an integer array nums, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
approachHint: Patience sorting with binary search (std::lower_bound) to build tails array in O(n log n).

title: Longest Common Subsequence (LCS)
statement: Given two strings text1 and text2, return the length of their longest common subsequence.
approachHint: 2D table: if chars match, dp[i][j] = 1 + dp[i-1][j-1]; else max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).

title: 0/1 Knapsack Problem
statement: Given weights and values of n items, put these items in a knapsack of capacity W to get maximum total value.
approachHint: Iterate items, then iterate capacity backwards from W down to weight[i] to reuse 1D array.

title: Edit Distance (Levenshtein Distance)
statement: Given two strings word1 and word2, return minimum number of operations (insert, delete, replace) to convert word1 to word2.
approachHint: If word1[i] == word2[j], cost 0; else 1 + min(insert dp[i][j-1], delete dp[i-1][j], replace dp[i-1][j-1]).

title: Unique Paths in Grid
statement: A robot on an m x n grid starts at top-left corner and moves only down or right. Find total unique paths to bottom-right.
approachHint: dp[j] = dp[j] + dp[j-1], or combination formula C(m+n-2, m-1).

title: Subsets (Power Set)
statement: Given an integer array nums of unique elements, return all possible subsets (the power set).
approachHint: Backtracking template: at each step, include nums[i], recurse, then pop nums[i] to backtrack.

title: Permutations of Array
statement: Given an array nums of distinct integers, return all possible permutations in any order.
approachHint: Swap elements into position index and recurse for index + 1, swapping back afterwards.

title: N-Queens Puzzle
statement: Place n queens on an n x n chessboard such that no two queens attack each other. Return all distinct solutions.
approachHint: Track occupied columns, positive diagonals (r + c), and negative diagonals (r - c) using sets.

title: Combination Sum
statement: Given an array of distinct integers candidates and a target, return all unique combinations where candidates sum to target (numbers can be used unlimited times).
approachHint: Sort candidates. When exploring candidate i, recurse with same index i (since reuse allowed) and target - candidates[i].

title: Activity Selection / Non-overlapping Intervals
statement: Given an array of intervals, find minimum number of intervals to remove to make the rest non-overlapping.
approachHint: Greedy choice: sort intervals by end time. Always keep interval with earliest finish time.

title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the kth largest element in the array.
approachHint: Maintain a Min-Heap of size k. The top of the heap is the kth largest element.

title: Top K Frequent Elements
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements in O(n) or O(n log k) time.
approachHint: Count frequencies in hash map. Use bucket sort where bucket index represents frequency.

title: Meeting Rooms II (Minimum Rooms Required)
statement: Given an array of meeting time intervals consisting of start and end times, find the minimum number of conference rooms required.
approachHint: Sort start times and end times separately, or use a Min-Heap tracking end times of ongoing meetings.

title: Single Number (Find Unique)
statement: Given a non-empty array of integers nums, every element appears twice except for one. Find that single one in linear time and constant space.
approachHint: XOR of a number with itself is 0, and XOR with 0 is the number. XOR all elements together.

title: Power of Two Check
statement: Given an integer n, return true if it is a power of two; otherwise, return false.
approachHint: A power of two in binary has exactly one bit set. Check n > 0 && (n & (n - 1)) == 0.

title: Number of 1 Bits (Hamming Weight)
statement: Write a function that takes the binary representation of a positive integer and returns the number of set bits ('1's) it has.
approachHint: Brian Kernighan's algorithm: loop while n > 0, clearing lowest set bit using n = n & (n - 1).
